title.narrative: SubResult 3.6 Technological Framework and Infrastructure reviewed and improved(Indicators:Existing Technological Framework reviewed and updated recommendations for spatial data sets and network services, etc. based on international technical standards given in the Tech. and Infra Report;The Technical Infrastructure, incl. the Prototype Geoportal, reviewed and updated with recommendations given in above Report;Information flows and data processing is prepared and given in above Report;Contribution to the development of online tools to explore spatial data with external stakeholders is given in above Report)

description.narrative: There is a need to review, expand and improve (if necessary) the existing Technological Framework and Infrastructure (incl. Geoportal) as it has been established through the help of beforementioned donors. The objective of a NSDI technological framework is to specify the requirements that the NSDI imposes on metadata, spatial data sets and network services, based on international technical standards or technical industry standards e.g. Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) and World Wide Web Consortium (W3C). The Technical Infrastructure is an information infrastructure based on open (geo) standards and adaptable spatial components, making it easy to find, access and reuse the data and services. Items such as the IT system architecture (including cloud computing), use of (inter)national (geo) standards; specific ICT components; key registries (single source, use multiple times); the Moldavans Geoportal; geodetic reference system; data quality and security management need to be reviewed and proposed and if exists redefined/confirmed.

comment.narrative: Technological and Infrastructure Report will be prepared under Twinning project.
Technological and Infrastructure Report prepared.

Activity 3.6.1 was implemented during 4th reporting period with one 5day mission in September 2021. Existing Technological Framework has been reviewed and expert provided recommendations for spatial data sets and network services etc. based on international technical standards. Activity 3.6.2 started during reporting period of QR1 earlier than anticipated in the project proposal on BC request. The reason is that the review of The Technical Infrastructure incl. the Prototype Geoportal was needed before drafting technical specification document for the development of the new NSDI Geoportal which was determined as BC priority considering that the procurement of the new Geoportal was planned in beginning of 2021. The methodology and schedule of the activity in the Initial work plan adapted to this BC need and four planned remote missions of MS STEs total of 40 working days have been conducted accordingly in order to review the technical infrastructure and draft technical specification document. Additional mission was implemented by two STEs in June 2021 to support the BC partners in preparation of bidding document. All produced documents under this activity are the bases for update of the Technical Infrastructure incl. the Geoportal. Activity 3.6.3 started in 7th reporting period with mission of two MS STEs in April 2022 total of 10 working days. During first mission MS STEs analysed how Moldovan NSDI stakeholders are creating data and are creating data flows among institutions. MS STEs prepared Guidelinesrecommendations for the information flows and data processing. The activity continued in 8th reporting period with mission in July 2022 and participation of three MS STEs total of 11 working days MS STEs finalized collecting and including information on information flows and data processing in Technological and Infrastructure Report. Also they analysed results from the questionnaire on data archiving.Activity 3.6.4 has started in 8th reporting period with mission in September 2022 and participation of two MS STEs total of 9 working days. MS STEs performed gap analysis of online tools to explore spatial data with external stakeholders presented examples from other European countries and provided recommendations for next steps for the ALRC.

title.narrative: SubResult 2.3 Business Model and Business Plan developed(Indicators:The easy to understand for all Stakeholders Business Model related to ALRC eservices and data is developed based on Result 2.1 and 2.2 and international experiences and presented and validated by the majority of Stakeholders;Then, based on above, the Business Plan for 1st upcoming budget year is developed and accepted by the NSDI User Council)

description.narrative: In order to promote the usage of the NSDI, its values and benefits must be known. Such a description may be provided by a Business Model. A Business Model describes the rationale of how an organisation creates, delivers and captures value. The focus of the NSDI Business Model is, as a consequence, on the value that the NSDI creates, how it is delivered and how the revenues are flowing. Usually, as a first step, a survey of existing financing and pricing models is initiated. Based on this survey, homogenous and simple models for financing and pricing has to be developed. In developing of Business Model and Business Plan the important elements are fees. It should also be taken into account that according to Article 14 of the INSPIRE directive (EC, 2007), discovery services and view services shall be provided free of charge. Under specific conditions, some view services may however be charged. Based on the developed Business Model, the Annual Business Plan(s) should be developed (as part of Strategic Plan).

comment.narrative: Business Model and Business Plan to be developed under Twinning project.
Business Model and Business Plan developed.

Activity 2.3.1 has started with mission of two STEs held in September 2022 total of 10 working days implemented. MS STEs objective during this first mission was to record the basic elements of the ALRC Business Model through methodology Business Model Canvas. The activity was finalized within 9th reporting period through two missions second mission by one MS STE in duration of 3 working days in October 2022 and third mission by 2 MS STEs in November 2022 total of 10 working days. Draft Business Model related to ALRC eservices and data was developed and sent to ALRC for their validation.Activity 2.3.2 was implemented in 10th reporting period through four missions total of 165 wds implemented. Within this activity Business Plan for upcoming budget year was developed based on the Business Model related to ALRC eservices. The Business Plan was shared with ALRC for their validation.

title.narrative: SubResult 2.2 Benefits identified (Indicators:Methodology document is drafted for benefits identification conform the EU practices and discussed with ALRC staff;The survey on benefits performed by the stakeholders; The Benefits Report with financial picture of direct and indirect benefits drafted based on developed Methodology (EU experiences and practices))

description.narrative: In the Member State Reports, submitted each third year to the European Commission, one chapter is devoted to cost and benefit aspects. Based on these reports, mainly the following division of benefits could be defined:Improved efficiency through reduced spending of resources;Improved effectiveness, better decisions, and better results;Other benefits.In many countries, exante CBAs (Cost Benefit Analysis) were performed in order to describe the financial implications of developing the NSDI and to implement the INSPIRE directive/NSDI. These estimates were then used as a motivation for specific investments in the NSDI, often supported by governmental grants.

comment.narrative: NSDI Benefits will be identified under Twinning project and Benefits report prepared.
NSDI Benefits identified under Twinning project and Benefits report prepared.

Activity 2.2.1 in order to draft methodology document for benefits identification in line with the EU practices started in 4th reporting period with one MS STEs mission in September 2021. The activity was continued during 5th reporting period with combined mission activities 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 of two MS STEs in November 2021. The methodology document is drafted as a part of the Report on benefits.The activity 2.2.2 started during 5th reporting period with combined mission activities 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 of two MS STEs in November 2021. The work on survey started by discussion on scope target group method and questions for the survey questionnaire. The questionnaire was drafted as a part of the methodology document within the Report on benefits. The activity was finalized during sixth reporting period with mission of two STEs total of 10 working days implemented in January 2022. During that mission the survey on benefits was performed by interviews with the stakeholders and distribution of questionnaire to additional stakeholders. Activity 2.2.3 was implemented in sixth reporting period with mission of two STEs total of 10 working days held in February 2022. Based on the received feedback from previous activities MS STEs in collaboration with their BC counterparts have drafted the NSDI benefits report with financial picture of direct and indirect benefits which was sent to the BC partners for their review and approval.

title.narrative: SubResult 2.1 Costs identified (Indicator:The clear financial picture of investments, their annual appreciation and annual running cost is assessed and presented in the Cost Report based on the accountancy procedures)

description.narrative: In general, the costs for establishing and maintenance of the NSDI are occurring among the data providers and the NSDI bodies, while benefits are often allocated to the users. The costs include elements such as preparing and entering metadata, transforming data sets for compliance with the INSPIRE data specifications, making data and services accessible through a discovery service (a national geoportal), viewing and downloading services, developing standard agreements and licenses for using the data sets and services, establishing and developing links with the egovernmental program, implementing technical standards, developing and specifying business models, providing support in data management issues, running and maintaining the NSDI geoportal and improving the skills and knowledge of people working with the NSDI. In addition, costs related to the coordination and management of the NSDI development are also included.Next to the direct costs, it is necessary to take external funding into account which is supposedly and mainly to be used for investments, and not for operational activities.

comment.narrative: NSDI costs will be identified within Twinning project.
NSDI costs identified.

Activity 2.1.1 started in December 2020 and continued in February 2021 during which questionnaire for NSDI costs identification was prepared and distributed to stakeholders. During 3rd reporting period additional mission was organized to assess received answers to questionnaire and to start drafting cost report. The feedback from six stakeholder institutions was received however some of it was incomplete so additional meetings were organized by MS STEs in order to be able to draft cost report. The Cost report was finalized during 4th reporting period within MS STE mission in September 2021.

The indicator and corresponding activity 5.1.4 were included with Addendum no 4 in order to support the strengthening of mapping and cadastre systems in the Republic of Moldova through its evaluation and provided recommendations for improvement. The activity started in QR11 and was finalized in QR12. MS experts focused on performing a comprehensive organisational strategic and legal overview of the cadastre mapping geoinformatics real estate valuation and land management and soil protection systems in the Republic of Moldova as well as review of organisations relevant for the functioning of the system. The findings and recommendations are included in report titled Evaluation of the status regarding mapping and cadastre systems in the Republic of Moldova and providing recommendations for their improvements. The document includes proposal for the organisational structure of the ALRC and of the geodetic cadastral mapping and geoinformatics administrative systems in the country. In addition experts prepared a proposal of the Government Decision for establishment of Agency for Geodesy Cartography and Cadastre as well as a proposal for the Statute of the public institution Real Estate Cadastre. The Government of the Republic of Moldova gave a positive opinion on the mentioned proposal and a comprehensive reformreorganisation of the system is in process as a result.

The indicator and corresponding activity 5.1.4 were included with Addendum no 4 in order to support the strengthening of mapping and cadastre systems in the Republic of Moldova through its evaluation and provided recommendations for improvement. The activity started in QR11 and was finalized in QR12. MS experts focused on performing a comprehensive organisational strategic and legal overview of the cadastre mapping geoinformatics real estate valuation and land management and soil protection systems in the Republic of Moldova as well as review of organisations relevant for the functioning of the system. The findings and recommendations are included in report titled Evaluation of the status regarding mapping and cadastre systems in the Republic of Moldova and providing recommendations for their improvements. The document includes proposal for the organisational structure of the ALRC and of the geodetic cadastral mapping and geoinformatics administrative systems in the country. In addition experts prepared a proposal of the Government Decision for establishment of Agency for Geodesy Cartography and Cadastre as well as a proposal for the Statute of the public institution Real Estate Cadastre. The Government of the Republic of Moldova gave a positive opinion on the mentioned proposal and a comprehensive reformreorganisation of the system is in process as a result.

Therefore, an awareness campaign based on a Communication Plan is needed. The role of modern webcommination tools, short video presentations, etc. needs to be seriously considered. The proposed target group consists of governmental ministries, state agencies, county administrations, cities, municipalities, nongovernmental organizations (NGO) and private enterprises. It is also requested to train and activate the so called local NSDI promoters on local level.
